# homeassistant/ — HA add-on packaging (Docker + nginx + bash)

*Generated by index-knowledge · commit 917d399 · branch main. See ../AGENTS.md for project-wide conventions.*

## OVERVIEW
Packs the SAME Next.js build into a Docker image that runs behind HA's ingress proxy as a sidebar panel — no app-side code changes; config is injected as URL params at startup. Images are published to GHCR by `.github/workflows/build.yaml`.

## FLOW
`config.yaml` (add-on manifest) → `run.sh` reads `/data/options.json` → builds a URL query string → templates it into `nginx.conf` → nginx :8099 proxies `next start` :3000 and rewrites asset paths with the ingress prefix.

## WHERE TO LOOK
| Task | Location |
|------|----------|
| Add an add-on option | `config.yaml` options+schema, `run.sh` add_param, `translations/en.yaml` label, `DOCS.md` table |
| Change injected URL params | `run.sh` add_param calls (must mirror what `app/page.tsx` reads) |
| Ingress asset-path rewriting | `nginx.conf` sub_filter rules (`/_next/`, `/api/`, `/favicon`) |
| Per-user monochrome | `nginx.conf` `map $http_x_remote_user_*` blocks + `run.sh` USER_MONO_MAP_ENTRIES awk injection |
| Image build | `Dockerfile` (2-stage) + `build.yaml` (build_from per arch) |

## GOTCHAS
- **`Dockerfile` uses `npm install`, NOT `npm ci`** — the macOS-generated lockfile lacks wasm32-wasi optional-dep entries and fails under alpine/musl.
- **Arch list is triplicated** — `config.yaml` `arch:`, `build.yaml` `build_from:`, and the workflow matrix must stay in sync (amd64 + aarch64 only; `node:24-alpine` has no armv7).
- The add-on `config.yaml` version drives the Docker image tag — SEPARATE from the integration's `manifest.json` version.
- nginx `sub_filter` needs identity encoding: `proxy_set_header Accept-Encoding ""` is required.
- Direct port 8099 bypasses HA auth AND per-user mono (which needs the ingress `X-Remote-User-*` header) — LAN-only.
- Don't write the literal `@@…@@` marker tokens in `nginx.conf` comments — `run.sh`'s sed/awk would substitute them and break the config.
- `run.sh` runs nginx + next together (`init: false`, no s6-overlay) and exits when either child does.
